answer_markdown:
## Taiwanese beef noodle soup

Here’s a cozy Taiwanese-style beef noodle soup for two, made with the ingredients you have. Simmer the broth until the beef is tender, then add the noodles and bok choy just before serving.

### Ingredients (for 2 servings, at Walmart)

- beef chuck: about 360 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- wheat noodles: about 200 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- beef stock: about 800 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- soy sauce: about 36 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- Huy Fong Chili Garlic Sauce 18 oz: about 20 g (substitute for doubanjiang, from Walmart)
- vegetable oil: about 10 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- tomato: about 90 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- onion: about 60 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- garlic: about 10 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- ginger: about 16 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- scallion: about 20 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- Great Value Ground Black Pepper 3 oz: about 0.4 g (substitute for Sichuan peppercorn, from Walmart)
- cinnamon: about 0.6 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- bay leaf: about 0.2 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- sugar: about 6 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- bok choy: about 120 g (common item, not checked against the catalog)
- ~~star anise~~: left out, no suitable substitute
- ~~Shaoxing wine~~: left out, no suitable substitute
- ~~pickled mustard greens~~: left out, no suitable substitute

### Substitutions

| Original | Use instead | Price | Taste / texture | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| doubanjiang | Huy Fong Chili Garlic Sauce 18 oz | $4.48 (unverified) | Adds chili heat, garlic, and a similar saucy texture, but lacks doubanjiang’s fermented bean depth. | A practical Walmart sauce stand-in; use a little less if you want to avoid making the broth too garlicky. |
| star anise | no substitute found (skip it) | | Skipping it leaves out the soup’s distinctive sweet licorice-like aroma. | No suitable spice was found in the store search. |
| Sichuan peppercorn | Great Value Ground Black Pepper 3 oz | $1.98 (unverified) | Adds peppery warmth, but not Sichuan peppercorn’s citrusy aroma or numbing tingle. | A weaker but available pepper substitute for a small amount in the broth. |
| Shaoxing wine | no substitute found (skip it) | | Skipping it loses some mellow, wine-like aroma in the broth. | Dry sherry, a common cooking substitute, was not found in the store search. |
| pickled mustard greens | no substitute found (skip it) | | Skipping them means missing their salty, sour crunch and contrast with the beef. | No suitable pickled vegetable was found in the store search. |

### Nutrition data used (USDA food for each ingredient)

- beef chuck: Beef, chuck for stew, separable lean and fat, choice, raw
- wheat noodles: Noodles, egg, dry, enriched
- beef stock: Soup, stock, beef, home-prepared
- soy sauce: Soy sauce made from soy (tamari)
- Huy Fong Chili Garlic Sauce 18 oz: Sauce, hot chile, sriracha
- vegetable oil: Oil, vegetable, soybean, refined
- tomato: Tomatoes, red, ripe, raw, year round average
- onion: Onions, raw
- garlic: Garlic, raw
- ginger: Ginger root, raw
- scallion: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb), raw
- Great Value Ground Black Pepper 3 oz: Spices, pepper, black
- cinnamon: Spices, cinnamon, ground
- bay leaf: Spices, bay leaf
- sugar: Sugars, granulated
- bok choy: Cabbage, chinese (pak-choi), raw

### Steps

1. Cut 360 g beef chuck into bite-size pieces. Chop 60 g onion, 90 g tomato, 10 g garlic, 16 g ginger, and 20 g scallion; set the scallion aside for serving.
2. Warm 10 g vegetable oil in a pot. Add the onion, garlic, and ginger and cook briefly until fragrant. Stir in 20 g Huy Fong Chili Garlic Sauce, then add the beef and brown it lightly.
3. Add the tomato, 36 g soy sauce, 800 g beef stock, 0.4 g ground black pepper, 0.6 g cinnamon, and 0.2 g bay leaf. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook until the beef is tender, about 1½–2 hours. Remove the bay leaf.
4. Cook 200 g wheat noodles according to their package directions. Add 120 g bok choy to the soup for the final few minutes, until just tender.
5. Divide the noodles between two bowls, ladle over the beef, bok choy, and broth, and finish with the reserved scallion.

### What will taste different

The chili garlic sauce brings heat and garlic but lacks doubanjiang’s fermented-bean depth. Black pepper gives warmth without Sichuan peppercorn’s citrusy aroma or numbing tingle. Omitting star anise, Shaoxing wine, and pickled mustard greens means the soup will miss some licorice-like aroma, mellow wine-like fragrance, and salty-sour crunch.

### Allergen check (avoiding: peanuts)

- Check the label: wheat noodles (processed food; allergens depend on the product label)
- Check the label: beef stock (processed food; allergens depend on the product label)
- Check the label: soy sauce (processed food; allergens depend on the product label)
- Check the label: vegetable oil (not in the catalog or keyword list; check the label)
- Check the label: bay leaf (not in the catalog or keyword list; check the label)
